chapter: Life in Columbus and recent activity
title: Capital University degree and film tribute

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: Okay, how long have you been going to Capital University?
Well this is my senior year this time, this year, 1980, so that has been 1976 was my freshman year.
So you're pretty close to a degree, huh?

Yeah, yeah. Well see my sickness, I had to fall out this last semester, so I have another year to go. But right now, I got my honorary degree, doctor's degree last year. Doctor of Musical Arts from Capital.
And this year, pardon me, they're doing two and a half hours of all the films that I had did up through the years and the contributions and all are going to a scholarship fund.
I read about that in Downbeat. Tell me more about that.

Well I thought it was a good idea, because Capital has been very good to me. All the faculty, the deans, and the president, just everybody, and I've enjoyed it. It's a very good music school and intimate it is, and it's a good school of learning, and I suggested this idea of doing, running these pictures for about two and a half hours, and we presented it to the president here, and he just loved the idea, and so that's what they're going to do.
And John Baker's supplying the film.
That's right, mmm hmmm. And so....
That'll be in a couple of weeks.
Yeah, the 27th is when it's showing, just before the semester closes.
The 27th of April. Yeah, that sounds great.
Yeah, I'm very pleased with it, looking forward to it.
What other movies can you recall, besides the ones we talked about, besides Make Mine Music and the Miller Story, and The Strip?
Well there was a couple I did there with Cab, short things.
Ten minute things.
Yeah. Then there was a couple I did there with Coleman Hawkins and Roy, just five minute things, ten minute things.
So you did some things with Coleman Hawkins and Roy Eldridge.

Roy. And a lot of things I did back there, them that they are going to show, I almost forgot about them when I saw them in John Baker's home. I looked and I said when the hell did I do that? And it was way back there that I had forgotten about them, because they were just short little movies, you know, short little shots, but very effective at the time, and they say it was very good.
I'm sure it'll be a lot of fun.
Very exciting, they say, the two hours is.
I wish I could see it.
Yeah, I wish so too.
